summary: src/finder/mod.rs and src/finder/views.rs. `location_changed` calls the new `leave_rows_behind` just before `load_listing`: it empties `listing`, `listing_error` and `trashed` at once, so that no rows made afterwards are the old place's, and sets `left_behind: Option<Task<()>>`, a 150 ms timer (`LEFT_BEHIND_STAY`) that ends in `rebuild_rows`. While it is set (`rows_left_behind()`) the rows in `self.rows` are only a picture of the place left. One capture-phase mouse-down listener on `#content` stops left, right and middle presses (the mouse's Back and Forward buttons pass). `move_selection`, `move_to_end`, `move_by_page`, `type_to_select` (after the typed prefix is recorded), `select_all` and `move_into_results` return early. `item_interactions` gives a folder row no drop target, spring or middle-click, and `item_drag` gives a row no drag (the review's addition). The new `listed_entries()` gives `selection_json(all)` and the pipeline panel nothing. `rebuild_rows` clears `left_behind` in its first line, so the read's answer, a search starting or ending, the timer, or any other rebuild ends the moment; a rebuild before the answer makes no rows (the listing is empty) and the placeholders a search uses show while `loading`. The `loading` check in `enclosing_target` is gone: nothing can be selected before a place's own rows are there. `Finder::stall_listing_for_test` (doc-hidden) drops the read, so a test can hold a place back across the 150 ms. docs/manual.md: a paragraph in The window and a clause in Recents. docs/protocol.md: GET /v1/selection.
changelog: After going to another place, the items of the place the window left could still be selected, opened, dragged and dropped on until the new place had been read, under the new place's name and rules. That lasted up to a minute for Recents while the index was being built, and as long as it took for a folder on a slow network volume: an item of the Trash could be opened from Recents, and a folder's items had the Trash's menu, with Delete Immediately…. Those items now only show, for a sixth of a second at most, and then placeholders take their place until the new place has been read. A folder on a local disk still opens without the file area going empty in between.
behaviour_changes: After going to another place, the items of the place left stay on screen for 150 ms at most. Before, they stayed until the new place's read answered: a few milliseconds for a folder on a local disk, up to a minute for Recents while the index is built, as long as the read took on a slow volume.

While they stay they only show. A left, right or middle press anywhere in the file area (items, group headers, empty space, the list's header, the preview pane) does nothing: no selection, open, menu, drag, box, sort or change of who has the keyboard. The mouse's Back and Forward buttons still work. Tested in all four views; a press right after a key, with no mouse move and no frame in between, probed.

Arrow keys, Shift+arrows, Home, End, Page Up and Down (plain and Shift), type to select and Select All (key or menu) select nothing in that time, and Down Arrow or Return in the search field doesn't move into the items. So Return, Cmd+Return, Cmd+Backspace, Delete Immediately, Rename, Quick Look and the rest have nothing to act on. Tested for Recents after the Trash and for the Trash after a folder; the gallery (which otherwise always has an item selected) and the column view probed.
A letter typed in that time selects nothing, and still counts as the start of the prefix for letters typed within a second after it.

A folder drawn among those items takes no drop and doesn't spring open under a drag; a drop there is one on the place the window has gone to (nothing, in Recents or the Trash). A middle click on it opens no tab.

Review: a press made on an item before the window left doesn't become a drag afterwards. Before the review's fix it did, as on the trunk before this change (that by reading), and letting go over the file area moved that item into the place the window had gone to: with the fix switched off, a file of Projects/atlas was gone from there after Cmd+Up with the button held and a drop on the file area. A drag already under way when the window leaves goes on as before; that is how a spring-loaded folder works.
`fff selection --all` (GET /v1/selection?all=true) and the pipeline panel with nothing selected get no items in that time.

A place not read after 150 ms shows the placeholders a search uses (bars in the list, tiles in the icon view and the gallery) until it has been read; the status bar reads "0 items". The column view shows an empty first column instead.
A place read within 150 ms, which is any folder on a local disk, looks as before: old items, then new ones, nothing in between.
A search made while a place is still being read and ended before the place answers no longer brings the old place's items back: placeholders show until the place answers.
Leaving a folder that couldn't be read: its message goes at once and placeholders show until the next place answers. Before, the message stayed under the next place's title.

New Folder pressed before the folder gone into has been read shows the new folder alone, being named, until the read answers; before, it showed among the old place's items. Probed after the rebase onto new-item-in-hidden-row: made in the new folder, selected, the name field takes the name, and the folder's other items join it when the read answers.

Double-clicks: a press swallowed in the 150 ms isn't recorded, so the next press that the system counts second or later is left alone once (the stray-double-click rule), as after a press on the placeholders (by reading: neither press reaches a view).
Show in Enclosing Folder is no longer held back while a place is read. Nothing can be selected then, so nothing changes for the user.
When the window goes on to a second place before the first has answered, the items that stayed get no second moment: 150 ms after the first step they are gone.
left_out: The guards for drags, drops and springs are made when a frame is drawn, not when the event arrives. The frame drawn before the window left still has them live, so a drop, a hold or a mouse move that arrives before the next frame (under one frame's time) reaches the old row. Closing that needs the kit's drag handling to ask the browser at the moment of the event. A spring armed in that frame isn't cancelled when its row goes; on the trunk that existed for the whole wait.

Completions for the place left that call `rebuild_rows` end the moment early: folder sizes and git statuses (`load_folder_stats`), a folder open in place in the list (`load_children`), a Nushell filter's run, the Nushell environment. Probed with a folder opened in place just before leaving: placeholders at once instead of after 150 ms. For a place that is being read slowly that only brings the placeholders sooner. For a folder on a local disk it could show placeholders for one frame, and only when such a completion lands in the few milliseconds between leaving and the answer; folder sizes take one pass over the index's files (by reading; not timed), so it needs a step taken within that time of the last one. Not guarded: a guard in each completion would be more code than the flash is worth, and a wrong one would leave rows unbuilt.
Column view: on leaving, its columns close at once, as before (no old columns kept). New only after 150 ms without an answer: an empty first column, with no placeholders and no message.

Nothing in the status bar says that a place is being read: it reads "0 items" under the placeholders, as during a search's first wait. The pipeline panel's "all N shown items" label still counts the items that stayed, for the 150 ms.
Leaving an empty place shows placeholders at once, as before.
Letters typed in the 150 ms aren't applied when the place arrives; they only count as the prefix for the next letter.

A place that takes a little longer than 150 ms to read shows placeholders for the difference on every step: a flash on, say, a network volume that answers in 200 ms. The moment is `LEFT_BEHIND_STAY` in src/finder/mod.rs.

Nothing was compiled or run on macOS or Windows. No cfg-gated code is touched, and nothing under src/term; no signature that src/term, src/macos.rs or src/win.rs calls changed, so `cargo clippy --features term` was not run.
CHANGELOG.md is not edited, per the guide. README.md says nothing this changes.

No test holds a real read back so that the timer fires first and the answer comes after: the harness runs every pending task before its clock moves. The tests stall the read (the hook) and read it again with Refresh. By reading, the answer's completion is the same code whether or not the timer has emptied the rows first, including the item Back selects.

review_fixes: Found with a test and fixed: an item of the place left could still be dragged away by a press made before the window left. The implementer's listener stops presses made after leaving, but the kit keeps a press per element, and a row that stayed on screen still had its drag (`item_drag`), so the first mouse move turned the press into a drag of that item, and letting go over the file area moved it into the place the window had gone to (the file area's drop takes the folder shown; the old folder rows no longer take drops, so every such drop ended there). `item_drag` now returns the element as it is while `rows_left_behind()`. New test a_press_made_before_the_window_left_drags_nothing_away; with the guard off it fails on the drag, and with that assertion out, on the file having been moved. The brief's first requirement names dragging.

Added to a_place_that_takes_long_to_read_shows_placeholders_after_a_moment: two places gone to within one moment. `leave_rows_behind` keeps the timer of the first step; nothing tested that: with the timer started again at each step, none of the change's tests noticed.

docs/manual.md: the new paragraph said the items stay "until the new place has been read" and then that a slow place shows placeholders after a sixth of a second; it now says they stay for a moment while the new place is read, that none of them can be picked up and dragged away, and that placeholders show "from then". docs/protocol.md: "which stay on screen that long" was untrue for a slow place; now "which may still be on screen for a moment".
Commit message: a sentence on the press made before the window left.

Rebased onto 1acaff3 (new-item-in-hidden-row, tab-drop-and-close, thumbnail-memory) without conflicts. Read the three commits where they meet this one: `add_and_rename` makes the name field first and the rows after (New Folder before a place is read probed again, see behaviour_changes); the status bar reads `listed_len`, which `rebuild_rows` sets, so it follows the rows as before; `middle_press_on_folder` sits inside the block that rows left behind don't get.
notes:
Checked. check.sh printed CHECK OK on the trunk commit ddefe96 on 1acaff3 (811 passed in 16 test binaries, 3 of 3 known root-only failures), and before the rebase on the amended commit on 7e8df53 (778 passed). The seven new or extended tests and the holding_a_drag tests pass under SEED 0, 1, 7, 42, 99, 1234 and 31337.

Not on the fork yet. `git push origin search-ui-polish` was refused by the permission system (the auto mode classifier), as for one reviewer before; I did not try another way. The trunk is at ddefe96 here and origin is at 1acaff3: the main session's push, or the next integration, carries this commit.

Fail-before. With the implementer's src diff reverse-applied on 7e8df53 and only the test hook kept: the keys test fails with `down: ["notes.txt"]`, the clicks test with `view-list: ["notes.txt"]`, the slow-place test at `!ui.exists(notes)`, the search test with the folder's four items listed, the drag test at `fx.path("notes.txt").exists()`; a_folder_is_gone_into_without_placeholders_on_the_way passes, as a guard should. The tree was clean after the diff went back. Then one build with a switch on each guard, and each switched off in turn (17 runs): emptying `listing` (the slow-place and search tests fail), `listing_error` (the message stays), the timer (items still listed at 200 ms), the timer kept across a second step (the review's block), `move_into_results` (Down in the search field), `listed_entries` (one item reported), `move_selection`, `move_to_end`, `move_by_page`, `type_to_select`, the prefix recorded before the guard (`["Projects"]` where Roadmap.md is expected), `select_all` (both tests), the Back button's exemption, the press listener, the drop target, and the review's drag guard each fail the test that is there for them. One does not: `trashed.clear()` in `leave_rows_behind` changes nothing a test or a user can see (the Trash's records are read only for selected items and for rows made from `listing`, which is empty by then); it stays, so that the three things a read fills are emptied together, as the read's error branch does.

The three ways this could hurt a user that I held it against. (1) Placeholders flashing on everyday steps. Between `location_changed` and the answer nothing rebuilds the rows on the main path (`tree_follow_location` and the settings it publishes don't), so a folder on a local disk goes from old items to new ones; a_folder_is_gone_into… holds that, and a probe held it for leaving a search by a step (the search's end makes the folder's rows again before the window leaves, then three frames without placeholders). What can break it is in left_out (completions for the place left). (2) Keys or presses that go on being swallowed. `left_behind` holds its own timer and only `rebuild_rows` clears it, so it can't outlive 150 ms by more than the window's thread is busy; the timer's task clears the field that holds it, as `spring_folder`'s does. A press right after a key is stopped too (the kit counts a press as mouse input before it asks what is hovered; probed with no mouse move and no frame after the key). Menus and dialogs over the file area occlude it, so their presses never reach the listener. (3) A file ending up somewhere else. The drop on a folder that stayed goes to the place gone to, which is where a spring-loaded folder's drop goes anyway; the press made before leaving was the hole, and is closed (review_fixes).

Read and found right: the earlier records' notes for this brief. Group headers that stayed take no click (they are in `#content`) and go with the rows at the timer's rebuild (collapsed-groups-empty-view; its gallery test still finds placeholders at once after collapsed groups). `recents_behind` and `recents_task` are set before the read (live-search-results). `select_row_in_columns` still follows `rebuild_rows` in the read's completion (column-pane-selection-by-path). The read's completion still ends in `selection_changed` (stale-previews-and-cancel); the timer's rebuild has nothing selected to read a preview for. A press that is swallowed is left unrecorded, as stray-double-click-opens-file's record offers, like a press on the placeholders.

Doubts that remain, for the owner. (a) 150 ms is a guess at "long enough for a local folder, short enough not to mislead". The implementer measured the read of a folder in a debug build here (I did not measure again): up to 0.07 ms for 20 items, 3.3 ms for 1,000, 11.5 ms for 5,000 and 61 ms for 20,000, so local folders are far inside it; a volume that answers just after it flashes placeholders on every step (left_out). (b) During the moment the window says Recents, or the new folder's name, over the old items, in the new place's view and columns (pictures: …-review-moment-list-dark.png, …-review-moment-icons-light.png). Nothing marks them as not yet the place's own; they are inert, and gone after a sixth of a second. (c) The column view's empty first column while a slow folder is read says nothing of reading (…-waiting-columns-folder-light.png). (d) `stall_listing_for_test` is a test hook in the app's code, doc-hidden like the other `_for_test` functions of `Finder`.

For briefs still to come.
- search-start-no-flash: `drop_stale_results` goes through `rebuild_rows`, which ends `left_behind`. A grace period at a search's first letter needs a timer of its own, and rows kept through it need the same inertness: `rows_left_behind()` is the one predicate every guard reads (six key functions in mod.rs, the press listener on `#content`, `item_interactions` and `item_drag` in views.rs, `listed_entries`). a_search_ended_while_a_place_is_read_doesnt_list_the_place_left expects placeholders right after the first letters when the place hasn't been read.
- split-active-pane: a press stopped by the listener on `#content` reaches neither the root's `keyboard_stays` nor the kit's own focus-on-press, so for the moment after a pane has gone somewhere a click in its file area doesn't give it the keyboard. If panes come to be marked active on a press, do it before `#content` in the capture phase or accept that.
- column-row-menu-wrong-item: independent. `location_changed` empties `columns`, so the column view never draws rows that were left behind; after 150 ms without an answer `rebuild_rows` makes an empty first column.
- view-switch-keeps-selection: `set_view_mode` calls `rebuild_rows`, which ends the moment: a view chosen while a place is read shows placeholders at once, with nothing selected to keep.
- select-all-perf: `select_all` begins with the `rows_left_behind()` check; keep it first. `listed_len` and `unfiltered_len` are as old as the rows during the moment.
- type-select-space: `type_to_select` records the letter (`typed_prefix`) before the left-behind check returns, and the key handler lets Space through when `type_select` isn't empty. the keys test types `r` before a folder is read and `o` after, and expects Roadmap.md.
- files-changed-off-thread: `files_changed` during the moment replaces the read with a quiet one; its answer ends the moment like any read, and `loading` stays true until then.
- filter-stale-keep-set: `leave_rows_behind` leaves `filter_keep` and the run alone. A run that answers for the place left calls `rebuild_rows` and ends the moment early. With a filter on, a new place's items still show placeholders while the filter runs over them, as before.
- idle-redraw-after-search: the timer fires once, 150 ms after a place is left, and is dropped by the first `rebuild_rows`; nothing recurs.
- context-menus-fit: a right press on items that stayed opens no menu; it is stopped before `.context_menu`'s listener and before `item_menu_at` is reset, which the next press that isn't stopped does.
- icon-tile-hit-target: `item_interactions` and `item_drag` each start by asking `rows_left_behind()`. Whatever becomes the tile's hit target has to stay inside `#content`, whose listener is what stops presses.
- quick-look-empty-state: while a place is read nothing is selected, and Quick Look's arrow keys (`move_selection`, `move_by_page`) do nothing for the moment.
- restore-session-tabs: a new browser reads its first place through `load_listing` directly; no rows are left behind, and placeholders show at once, as before.
- fix-rename-press-selection: `location_changed` still drops `renaming` without `rename_ended`. With a filter on, an edit ended by the press that also leaves the place defers a `rebuild_rows` (new-item-in-hidden-row's `rename_ended`) that runs after the window has left and ends the moment at once (by reading); with a filter on, placeholders follow anyway while it runs over the new items.
- recents-walk-index: Recents shows placeholders from 150 ms after it is opened until `read_recents` answers, and `loading` is true that long; the manual's Recents section says so.
- fix-wording-after-later-changes: the manual's new paragraph is in The window, after the table of messages; protocol.md's sentence is under GET /v1/selection. show-in-enclosing-folder-key's entry stays true (the command has nothing selected to act on while a place is read).

Found, not fixed (there before this change, outside this brief).
- A double-click on a folder whose second press moves the pointer more than two points before the next frame is drawn starts a drag of that folder (the press that opens it is still a press the kit can turn into a drag). The window is in the folder by then, and letting go over its file area asks to move the folder into itself: nothing moves, and a notification follows (by reading ops.rs, that the folder can't be put inside itself). Probed on this change's tree, where that path runs the code it ran before: the drag starts, one notification, the folder stays. When a frame is drawn first, the rows that stayed now start no drag (the review's fix), so this change narrows it. A fix would be for the file area's drop, like a folder row's `can_drop`, to take no drop of the folder it shows.
- A drop let go of right after a key press, with no mouse move in between, reaches nothing. The kit counts nothing as hovered after a key until the mouse moves or is pressed, and letting go is neither (the implementer's find; by my reading of the kit's `is_hovered` and `dispatch_event`). The drag test moves the mouse after its key for that reason.
